result.title: A balloon effect: ban one channel and a hidden trait finds another
result.comment: 30 pages, 9 figures, 2 Extended Data figures, 8 Extended Data tables; Supplementary Information included. Code and data: https://github.com/kkt94/balloon-effect
result.summary: Language models trained on the outputs of other models can acquire traits that those outputs never mention, such as a preference for an animal carried by lists of numbers. Such subliminal learning can pass on unwanted traits. The intuitive defence is to find and forbid the tokens through which a trait shows, but how a trait's trace behaves under such bans, and what of it a student learns, has not been resolved. We closed a trait's outlets one by one in two stress tests, a preference chain and a name chain, across two models, six output formats and 16 traits. Bans did not remove the trait. Much as squeezing a balloon in one place makes it bulge in another, the trait moved to wherever the format still allowed, an effect we call the balloon effect. Decomposing this transfer, which bans on surface features cannot stop, down to single heads and neurons, we show that it can be cut at the circuit that writes the trait into the output. Patching that circuit while the teacher writes numbers stopped the chains, sharply reduced the overt name leak and halved the trait passed to a student, whereas the same number of random heads produced no detectable reduction. These results give a mechanistic account of how unwanted hidden traits are transferred and a route to preventing it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究语言模型间的潜隐特质迁移：在多模型、多输出格式下逐一封禁表面通道，发现特质会转移到其他通道（「气球效应」），并通过定位与干预写出该特质的电路来削弱迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「封禁输出通道后隐藏信息改道」与电路级因果干预，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉或任务信息是真正被使用还是仅换路泄漏、以及贡献分配提供方法线索；但属纯文本设定，需核查迁移可行性。
